Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting
  of March 16, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the
  members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the
  day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
  Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the
  City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone -Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can
  participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l  If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are
  highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is requested
  that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however,
members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted
above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in
implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or
translation services in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable
modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-
412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org
no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  March 16, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, March 16, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint
  Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency  Members/Housing  Authority
  Members/Joint Powers  Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
  personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
  Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
  Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item
  Nos. 8, renewal of an agreement with Enerwise Global Technologies, Inc. dba
  CPower (CPower), and O-1, Adoption of Ordinance No. 21-05 granting Golden
  State Water Company a franchise to use or lay and use pipelines and
  appurtenances to transmit water. She also spoke concerning the feedback she
  receives when she calls.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item
  Nos. 4, adoption of Resolution No. 21-77, ratifying appointments to the South
  Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB), and 5, First Amendment to
  Agreement No. 20-169 with Environmental Science Associates (ESA).

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Padilla that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated March 12, 2021, in the amount of
  $5,066,611.14 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.
  1
   March 16, 2021

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  the following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Wanda Brown for alleged personal injury Whistleblower retaliation on
  September 15, 2020.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby reject claim listed as A1. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on
  July 21, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21-77 ADOPTED – RATIFYING APPOINTMENT TO
  THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB). Staff
  report dated March 16, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution ratifying the following appointment to the South Bay Workforce
  Investment Board (SBWIB):
  1. On February 23, 2021, the City of Hawthorne appointed Ms. Tonya Griffin,
  General Manager of Republic Services, to the SBWIB to serve a term of office
  ending June 30, 2025.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-77 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, RATIFYING AN APPOINTMENT
  MADE TO THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD
  BY MEMBER CITIES

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  AGREEMENT NO. 20-169 APPROVED - FIRST AMENDMENT TO
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL
  SCIENCE ASSOCIATES (ESA). Staff report dated March 16, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of a first amendment to Professional Services
  Agreement No. 20-169 with Environmental Science Associates (ESA) to extend
  the expiration date to December 31, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve the first amendment to
  Professional Services Agreement No. 20-169. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  THREE – YEAR BLANKET PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED -
  VISTA PAINT CORPORATION. Staff report dated March 16, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of a three-year blanket purchase order (with an
  option to extend for an additional year) with Vista Paint Corporation for the
  purchase of paint used for graffiti removal, per Bid No. RFB-0130.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member

  2
   March 16, 2021

  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve three-year blanket purchase
  order in an annual amount not to exceed $33,957 (total amount of $101,871). The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21-117 APPROVED - BATEMAN COMMUNITY
  LIVING, LLC DBA TRIO COMMUNITY MEALS; PAYMENT
  AUTHORIZED - BATEMAN COMMUNITY LIVING, LLC DBA TRIO
  COMMUNITY MEALS. Staff report dated March 16, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of a one-year agreement (with an option to renew
  annually up to three (3) years) with Bateman Community Living, LLC dba TRIO
  Community Meals to provide meals onsite for the Senior Nutrition Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-117 in
  an annual amount not to exceed $795,600; and 2) Authorize payment of invoices
  submitted by Bateman Community Living, LLC dba TRIO Community Meals for
  the time period of January 1, 2021 through and including March 28, 2021, for
  meals provided through the Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP) in an amount not to
  exceed $375,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 20-177 APPROVED - ENERWISE GLOBAL
  TECHNOLOGIES, INC., DBA CPOWER (CPOWER). Staff report dated
  March 16, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a renewal agreement
  with Enerwise Global Technologies, Inc., dba CPower (CPower), to serve as a
  Curtailment Service Provider for Southern California Edison’s (SCE) CAISO
  Capacity Bidding Program Addendum (CBP).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-177. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-118 APPROVED - INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY JOINT EXERCISE OF
  POWERS AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY. Staff report dated
  March 16, 2021, was presented recommending approval of the Inglewood Transit
  Connector Joint Powers Authority Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement (the “JPA
  Agreement”) with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (“Metro”) to form the Inglewood Transit Connector Joint Powers Authority (the
  “Authority”) to own, manage, and oversee the design, construction, financing,
  operation, and maintenance of the Inglewood Transit Connector Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve the Inglewood Transit
  Connector Joint Powers Authority Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement; and 2)
  Authorize the Mayor, City Manager, and/or designee to take such further actions
  incident to the execution of the JPA as are necessary to officially form and
  establish the Authority as a separate legal entity. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  ORDINANCE NO. 21-05 ADOPTED – FRANCHISE GRANTED TO
  GOLDEN STATE WATER COMPANY. Staff report recommending the
  adoption of Ordinance No. 21-05 to grant Golden State Water Company a
  franchise to use or lay and use pipelines and appurtenances for transmitting and

  3
 March 16, 2021

  distributing water under, along, across or upon the public streets, ways, alleys,
  and places within the City of Inglewood.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that Ordinance No. 21-05 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA GRANTING TO GOLDEN STATE
  WATER COMPANY, A CALIFORNIA CORPORATION, A
  FRANCHISE TO USE OR LAY AND USE PIPELINES AND
  APPURTENANCES FOR TRANSMITTING AND DISTRIBUTING
  WATER UNDER, ALONG, ACROSS OR UPON THE PUBLIC
  STREETS, WAYS, ALLEYS AND PLACES WITHIN THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD.

  which was introduced at the meeting held on March 9, 2021, be adopted. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at the hour of 2:40 p.m.

  Approved this 3rd day of August, 2021.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk
